title: Safely reconcile a vCenter VM CPU count after an ambiguous mutation
prompt:
Platform engineering needs a retry-safe way to converge a virtual machine on a requested CPU count when a mutating response may be ambiguous. Complete `VcfVcenterCpuReconciler/VcfVcenterCpuReconciler.psm1`.

Before implementing, research the `Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_get` and `Vcenter.Vm.Hardware.Cpu_update` operations in VMware's Apache-2.0 `vmware/vcf-api-specs` repository. Confirm their methods, paths, request and response models, documented statuses, and `vmware-api-session-id` authentication, and cite the source URLs consulted.

Keep the supplied manifest prerequisite on `VMware.Sdk.Vcf.SddcManager` version `13.5.0.25380678`; it supplies the OpenAPI server-connection contract used by the module. Do not install, download, copy, generate, vendor, intercept, or replace any VMware module, SDK assembly, binding, or OpenAPI file. Issue the requests as `System.Net.Http.HttpRequestMessage` messages sent through `System.Net.Http.HttpClient`; the implementation must not contain `Invoke-RestMethod`, `Invoke-WebRequest`, `Start-Process`, `curl`, or `Connect-VIServer`.

Preserve the supplied signatures and export exactly these commands:

- `New-VcfVcenterCpuClient` accepts either an authenticated `VMware.Sdk.OpenApi.Cmdlets.IServerConnection` with an optional `-Server` URI override, or the `-Server <uri> -SessionToken <string>` form. In the connection form, reuse the HTTP client returned by the connection's `.GetClient()` method. `-SkipCertificateCheck` belongs only to the token form. Creating a client performs no API request.
- `Set-VcfVmCpuCount -Client <object> -Vm <string> -Count <int64>` converges one VM on a positive CPU count.

For every invocation, first send `GET /api/vcenter/vm/{vm}/hardware/cpu`. Percent-encode the VM path value with `[uri]::EscapeDataString`. Reject a null or malformed successful response: `count`, `cores_per_socket`, `hot_add_enabled`, and `hot_remove_enabled` are all required; both counts must be positive integers and both flags must be booleans. If the returned count already equals `Count`, do not mutate. Return an object with `Vm`, `PreviousCount`, `Count`, and `Changed` set to `false`.

If the returned count differs, send exactly one `PATCH` to the same path with JSON media type and the compact body `{"count":<requested integer>}`. The update specification's `cores_per_socket`, `hot_add_enabled`, and `hot_remove_enabled` properties are unset and must be omitted, not sent as null, zero, an empty string, or false. On a successful PATCH return the same result shape with the observed old count, requested count, and `Changed` set to `true`.

Send `Accept: application/json`, authenticate with `vmware-api-session-id`, send no query string, and fail every non-2xx response. Do not blindly repeat a PATCH within an invocation after an error: the server may have applied the mutation even when its response was unsuccessful. A caller retry is safe because a fresh invocation performs GET again and skips PATCH once the desired count is observed.

Run `pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -NonInteractive -File tests/verify.ps1`. Do not modify the module manifest; edit only `VcfVcenterCpuReconciler/VcfVcenterCpuReconciler.psm1`.
scenario: the vCenter mock applies a count-only CPU update but returns HTTP 503, so a caller retry must re-read the VM, recognize the desired count, and avoid a duplicate mutation
constraint: the loopback fixture derives its sole path and two allowed methods from the protected contract, and its fsynced log proves the exact encoded target, headers, body bytes, one-mutation retry behavior, and omission of every unset update field
